title: Scales
description: Every scale the package publishes: its formula, its names, how confident the research is, and the sources that own the claims.

interval.description: A scale degree above the tonic: 1, b2, 2, #2, b3, 3, 4, b4, #4, b5, 5, #5, b6, 6, bb7, b7, 7, b8. b8 (a semitone below the octave) marks the final note of a non-octave scale like Σαμπάχ.

name.description: The scale's name in English, e.g. 'Ousak', 'harmonic minor'.

family.description: dromos: a Greek dromos. mode: a church mode. blues: a blues scale (6 notes).

intervals.description: Every note of the ascending scale, tonic first.

descending.description: Notes of the descending form, where it differs from the ascending one.

aliases.description: The names musicians use, per language. el: Greek; tr: Turkish (for the makam the dromos is named after or matches); en: English.

defaultTonic.description: The root the scale is conventionally taught on: D for the dromos (the bouzouki is tuned D-A-D), C for the major family, the modes, the major pentatonic and the major blues, A for the minor family, the minor pentatonic and the minor blues.

tonalName.description: The tonal library's name for the scale with the same intervals, if there is one.

tetrachords.description: How the scale is built, as two conjunct or disjunct units: the lower tetrachord (or pentachord) and the upper one. The units are named after the dromos or the generic family ('major', 'minor', 'hitzaz', …).

confidence.description: high: the sources agree and the 12-TET form is settled. medium: a rounding or naming convention is involved. low: the sources disagree, or the makam has a neutral pitch 12-TET cannot play.

caveats.description: microtonal: the original makam has intervals 12-TET frets cannot play. naming: the Greek name does not mean what the homonymous Turkish makam means. contested: the sources disagree on the formula. non-octave: the scale's upper octave is not a clean octave.

sameNotesAs.description: Ids of scales with exactly the same intervals (in the same order); the app links to them instead of duplicating content.

sources.description: Where each claim comes from; at least one per scale.

derivation.description: cited: the formula or fact is stated by the source (quote required). compositional: it is built from cited facts (explanation required).
